chunks: 28 - Allah's pleasure be upon him, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ta'i said: Abu Sa'id Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami al-Razi narrated from Ali ibn Ja'far al-Kufi, who said: I heard my master Ali ibn Muhammad say: My father Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them all).

And Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ishaq ibn Ja'far al-Alawi narrated to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi, from Ismail ibn Abu Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them); and the wording is for Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq.

A man from the people of Iraq entered upon the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: Inform us about our departure to the people of Syria, is it by a decree from Allah and destiny? The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: Yes, O Shaykh, by Allah, you did not ascend a hill nor descend into the depth of a valley except by a decree from Allah and destiny.

The Shaykh said: I account for my hardship before Allah, O Commander of the Faithful. He (peace be upon him) said: Hold back, O Shaykh, perhaps you think that the decree is irrevocable and the destiny is binding.

If that were so, then reward and punishment, command and prohibition, and restraint would be annulled. The meaning of threat and promise would vanish. There would be no blame upon the evil-doer, nor praise for the good-doer. The good-doer would be more worthy of blame than the sinner, and the sinner more worthy of praise than the good-doer.

That is the saying of the idol worshippers, the opponents of the Most Merciful, the predestinarians of this Ummah, and its Zoroastrians. O Shaykh, verily Allah, the Mighty and High, obliged with choice, forbade with warning, gave much for little, did not make the coerced disobey, nor the subjected obey, and did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain.
This is the assumption of those who disbelieve. Woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.

He said: The Shaykh rose while reciting: 'You are the Imam in whose obedience we hope, For forgiveness from the Merciful on the Day of Salvation. You clarified from our religion what was obscure, May your Lord reward you with good on our behalf.' 'There is no excuse in committing indecency, You rode it with disobedience and sin. No, no, nor the one who forbids it caused him to fall into it, If I serve, O people, it is Satan.' 'Nor did He love or will the disobedience, Nor kill the guardian with injustice and aggression. Indeed He loves, while His resolve is firm, The Possessor of the Throne, Allah declared that clearly.'
The compiler of this book said: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz mentioned in the end of this tradition only two couplets of this poetry from its beginning.

And Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farsi al-Aza'imi narrated this tradition to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rumayh al-Nisawi narrated to us in Jurjan, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ishaq ibn Ja'far narrated to us in Baghdad, saying: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Isa al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad al-Balawi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Nujayh narrated to us, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from their grandfather (peace be upon them).

And Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan also narrated this tradition to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: al-Abbas ibn Bakkar al-Dabbi narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhayli narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas.

He said: When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) returned from Siffin, a Shaykh who had witnessed the battle with him stood before him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, inform us about this journey of ours, is it by a decree from Allah and destiny? He mentioned the tradition exactly like the previous one.

Except that he added in it: The Shaykh said: O Commander of the Faithful, what are the decree and destiny that led us, and we did not descend into a valley nor ascend a hill except by them? The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The command is from Allah and the judgment.
Then he recited this verse: 'And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment.'
Meaning: The command of your Lord is that you do not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on Divine Decree (Qada' and Qadr) and Free Will?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through multiple chains including from Imam Ali (AS) and the Ahl al-Bayt, elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'Amr bayn al-Amrayn' (the matter between the two matters), rejecting both absolute predestination (Jabariyyah) and total free will (Qadariyyah). The Imam clarifies that while all events occur by Allah's decree, they are not forced compulsions, thereby preserving the validity of divine command, prohibition, and moral accountability. The inclusion of the verse regarding parents underscores that divine decree encompasses both cosmic events and specific moral injunctions, linking theological fate with practical human choice.
